scope: Preserve V8U through V9S, fit the separately published exit-door landing dimensions into the V9S qualitative normalized envelopes with one common relative scale, create deterministic low/base/high placement variants, and validate only transform reproducibility, envelope containment, topology and non-overlap.

A.basis: V9S envelope is wider than tall

C.basis: V9S envelope is wider than tall

B.basis: V9S envelope is taller than wide

model_hypotheses.common_relative_scale_rule: minimum over all stairs and axes of V9S envelope span divided by oriented published landing dimension

low.interpretation: lower-left residual-envelope placement; not a lower confidence bound

base.interpretation: centered residual-envelope placement; not a best estimate

high.interpretation: upper-right residual-envelope placement; not an upper confidence bound

contradictions_and_missing_information: The V9S envelopes are qualitative normalized unions of official-model graphics, not dimensioned as-built plans.
The 92 by 78 in and 116 by 78 in values describe landings by exit doors, not whole stair enclosures.
Orientation and low/base/high residual placements are explicit hypotheses.
Walls, doors, flights, treads, risers, stringers, attachments, exact metric coordinates, mass and component damage remain unresolved.

next_iteration.objective: Preserve V8U through V9T and test whether the geometry-only Floor 95 stairwell layer can be extended across Floors 93-99 using only the published V9R floor-band continuity and transfer topology. Create a categorical seven-floor stack only where continuity is supported, label every repeated placement hypothetical, preserve zero mass, stiffness, strength, connection and load-path credit, do not modify Blender, and do not run a structural solver.
